stories.title: Gov. Green discusses mental health policy at regional summits
stories.summary: Gov. Josh Green joined policy leaders in New Mexico and Utah to discuss mental health accessibility and insurance coverage. As chair of the Western Governors Association, Green is leading the Health Beyond Healthcare initiative. The sessions focused on state-level strategies for maternal mental health and disaster response.

stories.title: Optum studies pharmacy data for worker mental health risks
stories.summary: Optum is conducting a study using pharmacy records to identify correlations between mental health and workplace injuries. Chief Clinical Officer Tron Emptage said the research uses pharmacy data as a foundation to investigate cause and effect. The team is currently analyzing clinical data for potential risk indicators.

stories.title: Stress and anxiety are wearing workers down: How to spot your triggers and cope - Medical Xpress
Sudanese mental health professionals shift to remote care
stories.summary: A study in SSM Mental Health documents how Sudanese clinicians transitioned to digital care during a catastrophic breakdown of services. The move was described as a survival necessity rather than a planned innovation. Researchers interviewed nine professionals who sustained care across fractured supply lines.

stories.title: Maryland program provides free counseling for first responders' children
stories.summary: The First Responders Children’s Foundation and the Perdue Foundation have launched a mental health program for children of Maryland first responders. The initiative offers free, culturally competent counseling and parent coaching. Since 2022, the program reports it has supported more than 800 children across its network.

stories.title: UN hosts congress on burnout and the conscious pause
stories.summary: The Vacation Is A Human Right Foundation held its 4th International Congress at UN Headquarters to promote the conscious pause as a burnout prevention tool. President María Méndez advocated for a global culture of the practice, citing an unsustainable pace in contemporary society that leads to exhaustion.

stories.title: Study finds mental health gaps for refugees in India
stories.summary: A study of Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya refugees in India links mental health concerns to legal uncertainty and poor living conditions. Published in the International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care, the research calls for training community members to recognize psychological distress in protracted refugee situations.

stories.title: ConVal schools adopt peer-to-peer suicide prevention program
stories.summary: ConVal school district has implemented the Hope Squad program to promote mental health awareness and suicide prevention. The peer-to-peer model is funded by AmeriHealth Caritas New Hampshire and Monadnock Community Hospital. Advisers at three district schools received training to support students in identifying and discussing mental health needs.

stories.title: Anurag Kashyap's Son-In-Law Puts Ghee In His Eyes: What's Netra Tarpana? Ayurvedic Practice Explained - News18
Wellness expert suggests Yoga Nidra for mental balance
stories.summary: Roshani Shenazz, a wellness coach, suggests Yoga Nidra as a method to address persistent mental activity and difficulty relaxing. The practice, also known as yogic sleep, is presented as a guided relaxation technique intended to help individuals reconnect and find inner balance after daily responsibilities.

stories.title: NASA simulations study isolation effects on astronaut mental health
stories.summary: NASA is using its CHAPEA mission simulations to study how long-term isolation in confined spaces affects the mind. Researchers are examining the impact of separation from loved ones on stress management. The findings emphasize that human connection remains a critical component for maintaining emotional function during space travel.

stories.title: Author discusses holiday mental health and the role of conversation
stories.summary: Ray Greenstreet, author of Below the Breaking Point, suggests that silence is a primary challenge for mental health. In a recent interview, he advocated for open conversation as a tool for protection. The discussion focused on maintaining well-being as the holiday season approaches.

stories.title: Backdrop of Belfast provides the space for breathwork - ITVX
Hotpod Yoga updates class structure for strength and recovery
stories.summary: Hotpod Yoga has revamped its class formats to emphasize strength, recovery, and mental benefits. The company operates a network of over 65 studios with 500,000 customers. Its signature environment features a heated, dimly lit, and non-mirrored pod designed to support the physical and mental practice of yoga.

stories.title: Blanchelande College wins national mental health award
stories.summary: Blanchelande College received the ISA Innovation in Mental Health and Wellbeing Award at the 2026 Independent Schools Association ceremony. The school was selected from a shortlist of three. Vice Principal Dr. Vanessa Mitchell attributed the win to a community-wide commitment to ensuring students feel supported.

stories.title: Poor sleep after cesarean linked to postpartum depression
stories.summary: A study from Saitama Medical Center links poor sleep quality during the first 24 hours after an elective cesarean delivery to higher postpartum depression scores. Researchers analyzed records from patients who underwent procedures under neuraxial anesthesia. The findings suggest a correlation between immediate postoperative sleep disruption and later outcomes.

stories.title: Sleep hygiene program tested in Vietnam HIV clinic
stories.summary: A study at a primary HIV clinic in northern Vietnam suggests that integrating a structured sleep hygiene program into routine care is acceptable to patients and providers. Researchers identified sixteen facilitators and eleven barriers to implementation. The program focuses on behavioral practices to regulate sleep-wake cycles and bedroom environments.

stories.title: MIT study links brain waste clearance to aging
stories.summary: Researchers at MIT found that the process of flushing waste from the brain during sleep is commonly impaired in older adults. Participants aged 60 to 84 showed significantly smaller waves of cerebrospinal fluid compared to younger adults. The fluid is responsible for washing away toxic, memory-impairing proteins.

stories.title: Study links long sleep duration to heart disease mortality
stories.summary: A study of 3,287 American adults with heart disease suggests that sleeping nine hours or more daily is associated with a higher risk of death. Published in PLOS One, the research compared mortality rates across three sleep duration groups. Extra sleep may signal an underlying health problem.

stories.title: Wearable ultrasound patch tested for REM sleep
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Texas at Austin tested a wearable ultrasound patch designed to influence REM sleep. In a study of 28 participants, those using the device reached REM sleep 43 minutes earlier on average. The patch aims to affect sleep cycles without the use of medication.

stories.title: Consistent bedtimes could protect your heart health, new study - NewsNation
High-intensity yoga linked to improved sleep
stories.summary: A review of 30 randomized controlled trials suggests high-intensity yoga may be more effective for sleep disturbances than walking, resistance training, or tai chi. Researchers at Harbin Sport University analyzed data from 2,500 adults. The recommended regimen is yoga twice a week for eight to 10 weeks.

stories.title: Sleep apnea risk linked to lower grades in Jordanian students
stories.summary: A study of 1,798 students in Amman, Jordan, found that over one-fifth of primary children and one-quarter of adolescents exhibit symptoms of high risk for obstructive sleep apnea. High-risk screening scores were consistently associated with lower academic performance across school subjects in both public and private institutions.

stories.title: Meta-analysis identifies high-intensity yoga for sleep
stories.summary: Researchers at Harbin Sport University compared various exercise types to determine their effects on sleep disruption. A meta-analysis of 30 randomized controlled trials identified high-intensity yoga as having the strongest association with better sleep. The study suggests that not all forms of physical activity provide equal benefits.

stories.title: Study examines exercise intentions in fitness centers
stories.summary: A study of fitness center users in China found that exercise self-efficacy is the strongest psychological predictor of exercise intention and facility continuance. While indoor environmental quality was associated with comfort, self-efficacy showed significantly stronger links to behavioral intentions. The research addressed how facility environments influence sustained health behavior.

stories.title: Peggy Gou discusses fitness and travel
stories.summary: DJ and singer-songwriter Peggy Gou told GQ that she prioritizes fitness and gym access while traveling to maintain stamina and sleep quality. She incorporates daily workouts into her schedule regardless of her international tour commitments. Access to a good gym is a primary factor when she selects hotels.

stories.title: Jennifer Aniston discusses functional fitness method
stories.summary: Jennifer Aniston credits the PVOLVE functional fitness method for her mobility and stability. The routine focuses on twisting and reaching motions designed to build muscle mass and support bone density. Trainer Melanie Ramos notes the method is intended to translate directly to the movements of everyday life.

stories.title: 10-year-old completes 36 km open-water swim
stories.summary: Anvi Suvarna, a 10-year-old from Dombivli, completed a 36-km open-water swim from Dharamtar to Mumbai's Gateway of India in 8 hours, 34 minutes and 12 seconds. She carried a message regarding marine pollution and water conservation during the endurance swim, which lasted more than eight hours.

stories.title: Weightlifting may be more effective than other exercise at easing depression, study finds - The Eastleigh Voice
Runner shares story of life after 40
stories.summary: Graham Williams, a 59-year-old development manager, began running at age 40 after becoming a father. He has since completed multiple marathons and half-marathons. He credits the sport with providing motivation and a sense of achievement during his later career and personal life.

stories.title: Jennifer Lopez Reveals The Diet And Workout Routine That Keeps Her Fit At 57 - NDTV
Yoga practice linked to increased VO2 max
stories.summary: Research suggests that yoga can increase VO2 max by up to 11 percent. One study found that an hour of daily practice improved aerobic capacity. Instructors note that breathing techniques like pranayama may improve lung efficiency, offering an alternative to high-intensity cardiovascular workouts for some individuals.

stories.title: Nearly half of adults over 70 benefited from exercise training across several areas of physical function - Medical Xpres
MIND diet study finds no link to reduced mortality
stories.summary: A 20-year study of 15,000 adults in the Czech Republic and Poland found that the MIND diet was not linked to longer life after accounting for social factors. Researchers at University College London found only a small association between the diet and one measure of thinking skills.

stories.title: Peanuts and type 2 diabetes risk
stories.summary: A recent study suggests eating peanuts may be linked to a lower risk of type 2 diabetes by increasing fatty acids in the blood. Researchers note the association does not prove peanuts prevent the condition, and much of the benefit may be explained by body mass index.

stories.title: Sugary foods and breast cancer risk
stories.summary: A new study reports that women consuming more than two servings of certain sugary foods weekly faced a 28 percent higher risk of breast cancer. The findings showed no association with total sugar intake or fruit consumption. The study offers a statistic, but not a universal rule.

stories.title: Review finds no consistent harm in sugar substitutes
stories.summary: A narrative review in Nutrients examined the evidence on sugar substitutes regarding metabolic health and weight management. Researchers found no consistent evidence of harm across three major research consortia. The findings do not settle every question about the long-term effects of non-nutritive sweeteners.

stories.title: Study links meal timing to life expectancy
stories.summary: A study of 31,044 US adults suggests the timing of first and last daily calories may be linked to longevity. The findings show an association rather than proof that meal timing determines fate. The clock is now being asked to account for health outcomes.

stories.title: Concept analysis defines planetary health diet
stories.summary: A concept analysis in BMC Nutrition seeks to clarify the defining characteristics of the planetary health diet following the 2025 EAT-Lancet update. Researchers reviewed 69 articles to establish a framework for nursing practice. The diet remains a reference pattern designed for both human health and environmental sustainability.

stories.title: Endocrinologist explains blood sugar spikes
stories.summary: A lifestyle journalist explores the human experience through wellness and food narratives. The text details the author's approach to storytelling and her interest in everyday endeavours, but provides no information regarding blood sugar spikes or the endocrinologist mentioned in the title.

stories.title: Late eating linked to gut health in obese adults
stories.summary: A UTHealth Houston study of 87 adults with obesity links disrupted sleep and eating patterns to signs of a leaky gut. Participants who stayed up and ate later showed higher metabolic syndrome risk traits. Metabolic syndrome is a leading driver of cardiovascular disease.

stories.title: Makkah study finds obesity awareness gap
stories.summary: A clinical investigation in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, found that 37 percent of clinic attendees were overweight or obese. The study observed a disconnect between high levels of public health awareness regarding obesity and the actual physical habits of the participants. Knowledge is not always a daily practice.

stories.title: Toyota Sequoia leads SUV longevity rankings
stories.summary: An iSeeCars analysis of 51 million vehicles predicts the Toyota Sequoia has a 42.3 percent chance of reaching 250,000 miles. The average for all SUVs is 4.8 percent. The rankings provide a measure of potential ownership costs and resale value for shoppers.

stories.title: VO2 max in 70s may predict brain health
stories.summary: A long-term study tracked fitness levels, brain imaging, and cognitive performance to see if VO2 max in the 70s predicts brain health a decade later. The research builds on evidence that VO2 max serves as a marker for how well the body functions under stress.

stories.title: Healthy aging as a continuous process
stories.summary: A 2025 McKinsey survey found that 60 percent of consumers consider healthy aging a priority. Experts suggest aging is a continuous biological process rather than a single intervention. Consumers are increasingly looking for practical ways to preserve cognitive function and mobility over the long term.

stories.title: Tennis linked to longevity benefits
stories.summary: Research suggests recreational tennis may boost heart health, balance, and mood, potentially adding nearly 10 years to life. A sports medicine surgeon describes the sport as a full-body activity. The racket is now being positioned as a tool for longevity.

stories.title: GLP-1 medications and healthy aging
stories.summary: GLP-1 receptor agonists were historically framed as diabetes drugs that caused weight loss. Researchers are now investigating their role in a preventative, health-span-oriented approach to later life. Weight loss is increasingly viewed as one effect among several rather than the entire story.

stories.title: Americans spend more on healthspan
stories.summary: A 2026 Global Burden of Disease analysis found Americans spend an average of 14 years in poor health. While life expectancy rose by six months between 2009 and 2019, healthy life expectancy fell. Longevity is increasingly being distinguished from the years spent free of chronic disease.

stories.title: Coffee compounds linked to longevity
stories.summary: Researchers at Texas A&M used computer modeling to identify how coffee compounds interact with the NR4A1 receptor. The study suggests coffee's protective effects may stem from this molecular mechanism rather than caffeine. The receptor has been credited with the benefits.

stories.title: Seca targets longevity with body composition tools
stories.summary: Fitness operators are using medically validated body composition insights to track muscle health and metabolic function. The company seca is promoting these metrics as a way to differentiate wellness offerings. Longevity is now a measurable category for fitness businesses.

stories.title: Acupuncture in children shows low certainty
stories.summary: An umbrella review of 59 systematic reviews found that while acupuncture shows potential utility for pediatric illnesses, the findings remain constrained by methodological weaknesses. The research team from Sichuan University concluded that the evidence base currently offers low certainty.

stories.title: Naturopathy: Natural healing for a healthy India - DD News
Ayurvedic doctor opens boutique business in Kulgam
stories.summary: Dr. Fauzia, a trained ayurvedic doctor in Jammu and Kashmir, has launched a boutique business from home. Despite holding a Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery degree, she opted to pursue fashion and business to generate local employment. The stethoscope has been replaced by a sewing machine.

stories.title: Patanjali Ayurved promotes herbal knowledge at Herbal Kumbh
stories.summary: The Herbal Kumbh 2026 event in Uttarakhand combined an agriculture fair with a cultural festival to connect traditional herbal knowledge with farmers and visitors. Managing Director Acharya Balkrishna stated the initiative aims to bring people closer to plants and provide a wider platform for India's Ayurveda heritage.

stories.title: CII Global Ayurveda Summit discusses medical tourism
stories.summary: The CII Global Ayurveda Summit 2026 addressed the potential for medical tourism in Kerala. Industry reports suggest the state requires an additional 10,000 hospital beds to fully leverage current market opportunities. The sector continues to look for ways to expand its physical infrastructure.

stories.title: Ayurveda brands adopt gummy formats for wellness
stories.summary: Wellness companies are increasingly packaging Ayurvedic supplements as multivitamin gummies for children. The trend aims to simplify health routines by translating traditional ingredients into strawberry-flavoured treats. The industry is currently focused on making ancient remedies taste like confectionery.

stories.title: Magnetic therapy device market shows varied technology
stories.summary: The 2026 market for magnetic therapy devices includes products ranging from simple wristbands to powered systems that generate pulsed electromagnetic fields. Marketing for home-use mats and applicators remains optimistic. The category remains broad, as these devices use different methods to create their magnetic fields.

stories.title: Ayurveda Day reports high digital participation
stories.summary: The 11th Ayurveda Day recorded over 22,000 activities and 13 million supporters on its official digital platform. The Ministry of Ayush reported that participants documented their involvement through more than 90,000 submitted images. The theme for the global celebration was Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow.

stories.title: Ayurveda sector reports significant market growth
stories.summary: The Ministry of Ayush reports that the national Ayush market grew from 2.85 billion USD in 2014 to 43.4 billion USD in 2026. Efforts are now focused on aligning traditional knowledge with modern scientific research and international quality standards to support further global expansion.
